long_biography.plain_text:
A mechanical engineer's return to Samsun changed the scale of Robert Yüksel Yıldırım's family business. After graduate study in Oregon and five years designing container cranes in California, he joined its management in 1993. His first international move was direct coal importing from Russia, creating the trading income and maritime knowledge used to enter ports, shipping and bulk commodities. The acquisition of Eti Krom became a decisive industrial turn. Yıldırım and his brothers developed chrome mining and ferroalloys while adding container terminals, fertilisers, chemicals and logistics. Chrome and shipping became the businesses that made his fortune.

Yıldırım separated from the wider family enterprise and founded CoreX Holding in 2024. The new group preserves the mining and port businesses while expanding in nickel and other industrial sectors. He remains its chairman and chief executive. CoreX's mines, processing plants, terminals, vessels and corporate investments are group assets, not automatically Yıldırım's personal property. His football-club ownership is a separate sporting investment rather than the source of his industrial wealth.

uncertainties.detail: Robert Yüksel Yıldırım is the current full form used across Turkish corporate and university material. Some English pages omit diacritics or use only Yüksel Yıldırım. The dossier preserves Robert as the first name and normalises the middle and family names to Yüksel and Yıldırım.

Current CoreX material gives January 1960, while multiple official biographies give 1960 and Sivas. The stored 24 May 1961 derives from a Turkish Wikipedia-linked record. Month and year are corrected, but the day 24 remains unresolved because no authoritative source reviewed states a day.

Chrome and shipping are both directly documented as wealth engines. Metals & Mining is selected because Eti Krom and later ferroalloy acquisitions became the central industrial platform and remain the focus of CoreX's expansion; shipping and ports are material secondary businesses.

Yıldırım did not begin independently of family support: his father had an operating trading business and financed his overseas education. Self-made — advantaged start reflects that platform while recognising that Robert led the international coal trade, mining acquisitions and global diversification that created the later fortune. No source establishes an inheritance transfer as the primary mechanism.

Current CoreX material says Yıldırım left the wider family business and founded CoreX, while Bloomberg describes chrome and shipping businesses moving into the new holding. The dossier therefore uses CoreX for current primary industry and avoids treating historical group-wide interests as unchanged personal holdings.

Mines, processing plants, port concessions, vessels, corporate stakes, employee counts, revenue and investment budgets belong to CoreX or its operating companies. They are not attributed directly to Yıldırım's personal balance sheet.
The LinkedIn, X and current CoreX company profile meet the threshold. No exact personal Instagram, Personal Website, Facebook, YouTube, TikTok or dedicated Forbes profile was verified.

Politics, controversies, allegations, legal matters, sanctions, private-family trivia and vessel-specific research are excluded. Football ownership appears only to distinguish a separate sporting interest from industrial wealth.
